First release: the Securo personal finance manager as one container you can install from a template, on Securo 0.16.3.

## ✨ Added

- The official `securo-backend` and `securo-frontend` images of the same version in one container. nginx serves the web app on port 8080 and passes `/api/` to the backend, and the Celery worker and scheduler run next to it, so bank syncs, recurring transactions and price updates need no extra containers.
- Your own PostgreSQL and Redis are the default. On the first start Securo creates its database and enables pgvector there, if the user may.
- `BUILTIN_POSTGRES=true` runs PostgreSQL 16 with pgvector inside the container, with its data in `/data/postgres`, listening only on `127.0.0.1`. An interrupted first start leaves no half-made database behind.
- `BUILTIN_REDIS=true` runs Redis inside the container, with a snapshot in `/data/redis`.
- The secret key and the password of the built-in database are generated on the first start and kept in `secrets.env` in the data folder. A secret key set in the template wins.
- A missing database or Redis host, a refused password or a PostgreSQL without pgvector ends in one line in the log that says what to change.
- Attachments and the built-in databases in the data folder belong to `PUID:PGID` (99:100 by default).
- The settings from upstream's `.env.example`, apart from the AI agents, work as container variables under the same names, and the template carries the ones for bank sync and OIDC sign-in.
- `SECURO IS READY` in the log once the first start with its migrations has finished, and a health check on `/api/health`.
- Images for linux/amd64 and linux/arm64.
- Every build starts the image with the built-in databases, signs up, stores an account, restarts and finds it again. It also signs up against an external PostgreSQL with pgvector and a Redis with a password.

## 🎨 Design

- README with download buttons for Unraid, Docker and the source, and the web app pictured in dark mode inside a browser window.
